items.claim: Absence of an anti-forgery (CSRF) token on a state-changing request is the observable precondition that makes cross-site request forgery possible against that endpoint.
items.body:
Absence of an anti-forgery (CSRF) token on a state-changing request is the observable precondition that makes cross-site request forgery possible against that endpoint.

items.claim: Once a state-changing endpoint is found to lack an anti-CSRF token, an attacker can host an auto-submitting cross-site form that repoints an account email to an address the attacker controls, using only the victim's ambient session.

items.claim: An anti-CSRF token can be cleared by hammering it with length-validation, null-value, and array-value manipulation; a token that rejects all three is not vulnerable to those bypass families.
items.body:

items.claim: Switching the HTTP request method and blanking the CSRF token are the two standard bypass probes for a token-protected state change; when both are rejected the token handling is not the weak link and other same-site protections must be examined.
items.body:
Switching the HTTP request method and blanking the CSRF token are the two standard bypass probes for a token-protected state change; when both are rejected the token handling is not the weak link and other same-site protections must be examined.

items.disproof: Either changing the request method or sending the request with the CSRF token parameter removed/emptied still changes state, proving the token is not enforced.
